FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–6 YEARS

Nature Club Animals flashcards.

Twenty-two spotter sheets for children who already know their animal families and want to go deeper — this is the Nature Club deck, the step up from Animal Categories. Each card studies one specialist group: the hunters of the sky, the shells of the shore, the animals that pollinate our food, the whole dog family from wolf to dingo, and the wild homes from grassland to mountaintop. Each card page carries a simple guide a kid can follow, and every card opens its own Nature Club lesson on its own page.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Each card has its own page, and every card shows its age pill — start with the group that fits your child today.

Birds of the world

The hunters and the singers of the sky: the raptors with their sharp eyes, the birds at the backyard feeder, the desert’s roadrunners and the strange birds of Australia.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    The Spotter's Walk

    Take one card on your walk — birds-of-prey on the park day, garden-birds any day — and count what you actually spot from its squares. Real animals are everywhere once you have a card in your pocket.

  2. 02

    The deeper deck

    This set steps up from Animal Categories: same two-by-two sheets, closer study. Read one square a day and ask "how is this animal different from its cousin beside it?" A hawk and a falcon look alike — until they don’t.

  3. 03

    Same animal, two names

    The cards carry the ocean-crossing names: the reindeer of Lapland is the caribou of Canada, a prawn in Britain is a shrimp in America, and a buzzard means two different birds on two sides of the Atlantic. Both names are right.

  4. 04

    Family tree game

    Lay the dog-family card beside the pets card: which animals are cousins? Then rodents beside small-animals, garden-birds beside birds. The deeper deck keeps meeting the first deck — cousins everywhere.

  5. 05

    Draw the one you met

    After a spotting walk, draw the real creature you saw next to the card version. A notebook of met animals is the Nature Club badge of honor — one page per walk, no rush.
